fixed: "Neighbor Roll Away" and "Partners roll away" now come in as a roll away with your neighbor or partner, instead of one where the neighbors roll each other away. "Neighbor rollaway w/ half sashay", as Caller's Companion writes it, now comes in as a roll away too, and a note like "(Robins roll R, Larks step L)" sets who rolls the others away. This applies to imports and to figures you type; figures you already imported are unchanged.
An imported box circulate that has a line to itself now includes its balance in 8 beats and leaves it out in 4. Before, every box circulate showed a balance.
A Caller's Box line that names its subject in a leading bracket, such as "[Ones] Box circulate", no longer shows that subject as assumed.

changed: The shared figure recognizer, and the ContraDB dialect for a line with one dancer set, read a relationship that is the line's only dancer set as roll_away's whom, leaving who to the default with assumedSubject; the recognizer also reads "rollaway" and "w/ half sashay".
withBeatImpliedBalance sets box_circulate's balance from a whole line's beats (8: true, 4: false) in the Caller's Companion mapper, the Caller's Box per-line parse and reparseImportGapFigures.

The CallersBox per-role roll-away annotation fills who on the whom reading for any roll-away relationship and clears assumedSubject; it also reads a role-named note ("role2s roll R, role1s step L"). A leading bracket that fills who clears assumedSubject, and does not overrule an annotation's roller.
